Pete Hitchcock, Clive Shippen and Len Bishop were next, in the 170's while the rest of our men were back in the 200's. The next view of the field was soon after the first lap had ended, and Walker had moved up to Gebbett and Short and Moore had also progressed about fifteen places and were running well.

A spectacular return to form by Charlie Dabbs, a defiant battle against "father time" and injuries successfully overcome by Archie Bedford, and an extraordinary run by Clive Shippen were just a few of the highlights to emerge from this event, considered by some to be an unofficial "Brighton" trial.
Approaching the end of the first lap Miller, Thompson, Glover, Bedford and Shippen were in close attendance around tenth position with John Moore moving through fast after his mishap.
Mike Maynard set a fast pace at the start and was comfortably leading after a mile from John Moore and Chris Thompson with Clive Shippen and the Blackheath captain, A.W.
Jim Heathfield took over from Collis on the second stage for the 'D' team with Bhatia running for the 'A', Shippen for the 'C' and Conway for the 'E'.

The first major cross-country race, the South of the Thames Junior, was held at Epsom Downs on November 8th and Ken Miller(20th), John Moore(26th), Malcolm Robinson(34th) and Clive Shippen(35th) ran well to give us 3rd team award behind South London and Walton.
Jim Heathfield could not hold this place under heavy pressure and dropped back to sixth and handed over to Clive Shippen forty seven seconds in arrears.

Clive Shippen, now almost fit again, held fifth place without losing ground on Woodford and handed over to Don Maclean for the final leg fifty seconds down on T.V.H. and thirty-three down on Woodford Green A.C.
Our first team,made up of Shippen, Black, Walker, Robinson, Stearman and Moore wandered between thirteenth and ninth before settling in tenth place- a position far below their capabilities.
Gordon was well backed up by Shipley (3rd), Maclean & Shippen (6th), Forey (8th) and Miller (12th).
